report.headline: The ACCELERATE trial of evacetrapib was stopped for futility in ~12,092 high-risk vascular patients, confirming that CETP inhibition does not reduce cardiovascular events despite large HDL-C increases.
report.summary: ACCELERATE randomized 12,092–12,095 patients with high-risk vascular disease to evacetrapib 130 mg daily or placebo on top of statin therapy. The primary endpoint was a composite of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, coronary revascularization, or hospitalization for unstable angina, with 1,670 planned events. After a median follow-up of 1.5 years, an independent DSMB recommended stopping the trial for futility on October 12, 2015, with no safety signal. Phase 2 data showed evacetrapib raised HDL-C by 103% (placebo-adjusted) and lowered LDL-C by 15% (placebo-adjusted, −0.56 mmol/L). The calculator, using the LDL-C reduction and 1.5-year follow-up, predicted only a 5.7% relative risk reduction (HR 0.943) and 22% power to detect it. The observed result was neutral (HR ~1.01). The failure is best explained by the intended biomarker (HDL-C) not being causally protective for coronary disease, consistent with Mendelian randomization evidence. Genetic support for CETP as a target was uncertain (association score 0.736, zero evidence items before the trial cutoff). No off-target harm was detected (no QT prolongation, no clinically relevant blood pressure effect at therapeutic doses).
key_evidence: 12,092–12,095 patients randomized (Lilly to Discontinue Development of Evacetrapib for High-Risk Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease (Oct 12, 2015); ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01687998 ACCELERATE; Assessment of the clinical effects of cholesteryl ester transfer protein inhibition with evacetrapib in patients at high-risk for vascular outcomes: Rationale and design of the ACCELERATE trial.)

1,670 planned primary endpoint events (Assessment of the clinical effects of cholesteryl ester transfer protein inhibition with evacetrapib in patients at high-risk for vascular outcomes: Rationale and design of the ACCELERATE trial.)

Median follow-up 1.5 years (Assessment of the clinical effects of cholesteryl ester transfer protein inhibition with evacetrapib in patients at high-risk for vascular outcomes: Rationale and design of the ACCELERATE trial.)

Phase 2: evacetrapib increased HDL-C 103% placebo-adjusted (Efficacy, safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetic profile of evacetrapib administered as monotherapy or in combination with atorvastatin in Japanese patients with dyslipidemia.) and 129% in phase 3 design (Assessment of the clinical effects of cholesteryl ester transfer protein inhibition with evacetrapib in patients at high-risk for vascular outcomes: Rationale and design of the ACCELERATE trial.)

Phase 2: placebo-adjusted LDL-C lowering −15% (−0.56 mmol/L from baseline 144.3 mg/dL) (Efficacy, safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetic profile of evacetrapib administered as monotherapy or in combination with atorvastatin in Japanese patients with dyslipidemia.; Effects of the CETP inhibitor evacetrapib administered as monotherapy or in combination with statins on HDL and LDL cholesterol: a randomized controlled trial.; The pharmacokinetics and pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic relationships of evacetrapib administered as monotherapy or in combination with statins.)
Calculator predicted 22% probability of success (HR 0.943, 5.7% RRR) based on LDL-C reduction; trial stopped for futility (Calculator; Verdict)
CETP genetic association score 0.736 (uncertain) with zero genetic evidence items before 2015-10-12 (opentargets:CETP)

No off-target harm: no QT prolongation (Evacetrapib at a supratherapeutic steady state concentration does not prolong QT in a thorough QT/QTc study in healthy participants.); no clinically relevant BP effect at therapeutic doses (Efficacy, safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetic profile of evacetrapib administered as monotherapy or in combination with atorvastatin in Japanese patients with dyslipidemia.); SBP +1.69 mmHg only at supratherapeutic dose (Effects of the cholesteryl ester transfer protein inhibitor evacetrapib on lipoproteins, apolipoproteins and 24-h ambulatory blood pressure in healthy adults.)
report.what_would_change_this: A trial powered for a 5–6% RRR would require ~50,000 patients and 4+ years of follow-up, which is not feasible for this mechanism. Only evidence that HDL-C elevation is causally protective (contradicting current Mendelian randomization data) or a CETP inhibitor with substantially greater LDL-C lowering and longer exposure (as seen with anacetrapib in REVEAL) could alter the conclusion.
report.readthrough_note: Other CETP inhibitors have shown mixed results: torcetrapib caused harm, dalcetrapib failed for futility, and anacetrapib demonstrated a modest 9% RRR (HR 0.91) only after median 4.1 years of follow-up in REVEAL, driven by larger LDL-C lowering. This pattern suggests CETP inhibition may require greater LDL-C reduction and longer duration to translate into clinical benefit.

for.text: The intended biomarker was HDL-C. Phase 2 showed 103% placebo-adjusted increase at 12 weeks with 100 mg + atorvastatin 10 mg (f_9bd89b71fca798). Phase 3 confirmed large HDL-C elevation (129% per f_02746d884f6ab5). However, Mendelian randomization and genetic evidence consistently show HDL-C is not causally protective for coronary heart disease.
The calculator itself used LDL-C (not HDL-C) as the basis for expected HR, acknowledging HDL-C is non-causal (basis: "LDL-C").

against.text: LDL-C was also lowered (-15% placebo-adjusted in phase 2, f_c9a0169cf137ab), and LDL-C is causal. The expected HR from LDL-C lowering alone was 0.943.

hypotheses.would_settle: Mendelian randomization studies of CETP variants on CVD outcomes (e.g., Voight et al. 2012, Holmes et al. 2015) already establish HDL-C is not causal; no further trial data needed.

for.text: Using the causal biomarker (LDL-C), the phase 2 placebo-adjusted change was -0.56 mmol/L (-15% from 3.731 mmol/L baseline). With 1.5-year median follow-up (time_factor 0.575), expected HR = 0.943 (5.7% RRR). Trial had only 22% power to detect this; MDE at 80% power was HR 0.872.
Planned events (1670) and sample size (12,092) were sized for a larger effect; the observed HR was ~1.01 (neutral).

against.text: If HDL-C were causal, the biomarker effect was enormous (103% increase) and would have predicted a large benefit.

hypotheses.would_settle: A trial powered for a 5-6% RRR would need ~50,000 patients and 4+ years follow-up; not feasible for this mechanism.

for.text: CETP genetic association score is 0.736 (uncertain) with only 13 evidence items (f_ff8d155f87441a). Previous CETP inhibitors failed: torcetrapib (harm), dalcetrapib (futility), anacetrapib (modest benefit only in REVEAL after 4+ years).
The calculator flags "target genetics: uncertain" as the weakest link.

against.text: Anacetrapib (REVEAL) showed a 9% RRR (HR 0.91) after median 4.1 years, suggesting CETP inhibition can work with longer exposure and larger LDL-C lowering.

hypotheses.would_settle: Longer-term outcome data from REVEAL (anacetrapib) and genetic studies of CETP loss-of-function variants.

for.text: Phase 2 showed +1.69 mmHg SBP increase at 600 mg (supratherapeutic) Day 14 (f_73f043d9486743), translating to HR 1.022 harm factor.

against.text: No clinically relevant BP effect at therapeutic doses (f_786c481b4f5067: "not likely to be associated with any significant change in blood pressure" at 100 mg + atorvastatin). No QT prolongation (f_c23a5e6fd2420b). No mineralocorticoid/glucocorticoid effects (f_5569a44aa98530, f_786c481b4f5067). Phase 3 safety signal false (f_c6022efac3361f).

hypotheses.would_settle: BP data from phase 3 at 130 mg dose; already available and neutral.

for.text: High-risk vascular disease patients on background statin therapy — appropriate for secondary prevention.

against.text: No evidence of wrong population; inclusion criteria standard for CVOT (f_84aa78e606ac9d, f_93107b6fbdf92d, f_dc9ce380d87d9a).

hypotheses.would_settle: Subgroup analyses by baseline LDL-C, HDL-C, or statin intensity — already planned/available.

for.text: Composite endpoint includes coronary revascularization (softer component), but this is standard for CVOTs. Median follow-up 1.5 years (f_13d6532df5671c) may be short for atherosclerosis modification.

against.text: Event-driven design with 1670 planned events (f_7262d7298b3588) is standard. Revascularization inclusion increases event rate but dilutes specificity; however, hard endpoints (CV death, MI, stroke) also neutral.

hypotheses.would_settle: Longer follow-up (as in REVEAL) to assess hard endpoints separately.

for.text: Trial stopped early for futility (announcement:accelerate 2015-10-12), not safety or enrollment issues.

against.text: Well-executed: 12,092 randomized (f_12844a82cf3808), high adherence implied by biomarker changes, no safety signals, independent DSMB recommended stop for futility.

issues.issue: Verifier could not confirm the LDL-C -15% change for the combination regimen (100 mg evacetrapib + atorvastatin 10 mg). The verified fact f_c9a0169cf137ab claims this combination, but the verifier's SQL query returned monotherapy data (15% at 100 mg monotherapy vs placebo). Since LDL-C is the basis for the calculator's expected HR (0.923), this discrepancy must be resolved.
issues.request: Re-check the source (pmid:24786356) for the LDL-C change: confirm whether the -15% at 100 mg is from the combination-with-atorvastatin arm or the monotherapy arm. If it is monotherapy, update the calculator input to reflect the correct regimen and re-run.

issues.issue: Automatic checks flag HDL-C abs_change=1.468 and LDL-C abs_change=-0.56 as not matching cited facts. These absolute changes are computed from percent change × baseline (both verified). The flags appear to be false positives because the registry stores percent changes and baselines separately, not absolute changes. However, the calculator inputs should explicitly note the computation in the method field for traceability.
issues.request: Add a note in the calculator input method fields (e.g., 'abs_change_computed_from_pct_and_baseline') to clarify the derivation and prevent false-positive flags.

issues.issue: Hypotheses reference 'calculator' as a citation for quantitative claims (expected HR, power, MDE). Per style, cite the specific calculator output fields (e.g., 'calculator.expected_hr', 'calculator.power') rather than the generic term.
issues.request: Update hypothesis 'for' entries to reference specific calculator output keys (expected_hr, power, mde_hr_80) instead of just 'calculator'.

issues.issue: The apoB change (-28.56% at 600 mg, Day 14, placebo-adjusted) is available in verified facts (f_b80b4ed20c7c5c) but not included in calculator inputs. While the calculator uses LDL-C as the causal basis, apoB is a stronger causal biomarker and could provide a cross-check. Its absence is not an error but a missed opportunity for triangulation.
issues.request: Consider adding apoB as a secondary biomarker input (with appropriate caveats: higher dose, shorter duration) to see if the expected HR changes materially.

issues.issue: apoB input cites f_b80b4ed20c7c5c but that verified fact is for LDL-C (-28.56% at 600 mg), not apoB. The calculator input says biomarker: "apoB" with pct_change: -28.56, source: pmcid:PMC4284021 (which is f_b80b4ed20c7c5c). No verified fact for apoB change exists in the provided list. This is a biomarker mismatch.
issues.request: Correct the apoB input: either find a verified apoB change fact from pmcid:PMC4284021 or remove the apoB entry if no reliable placebo-adjusted phase 2 apoB data exists at the relevant dose.

issues.issue: HDL-C 103% change (f_9bd89b71fca798) is labeled "placebo_adjusted": true in verified facts, but Verifier SQL query found the comparator was atorvastatin alone (active), not placebo. The calculator input method says "phase2_placebo_adjusted_combination_statin_12wk_100mg". This discrepancy matters: if the 103% is vs active comparator (atorvastatin), it is not placebo-adjusted and may overstate the incremental effect of evacetrapib.
issues.request: Clarify whether f_9bd89b71fca798 is truly placebo-adjusted or active-comparator-adjusted. Search the source (pmid:24786356) for the exact comparison group. If it's vs atorvastatin alone, change method to "phase2_active_comparator_adjusted_combination_statin_12wk_100mg" and adjust interpretation.

issues.issue: LDL-C -15% change (f_c9a0169cf137ab) verified fact states dose "100 mg + atorvastatin 10 mg" and placebo_adjusted: true, but Verifier SQL query returned monotherapy data (evacetrapib monotherapy vs placebo). The calculator input assumes combination regimen. Need to resolve whether the -15% is for combination or monotherapy.
issues.request: Check pmid:24786356 for the exact LDL-C comparison: is the -15% for evacetrapib 100 mg + atorvastatin 10 mg vs placebo + atorvastatin 10 mg, or evacetrapib 100 mg monotherapy vs placebo? Update method tag accordingly.

issues.issue: apoB input has baseline: null and abs_change: null. While percent change alone can be used, the calculator may need baseline for absolute change calculations or for cross-biomarker scaling. If apoB data is kept, a baseline value should be sourced from the same study.
issues.request: If apoB change is retained, find baseline apoB from the same phase 2 study (pmcid:PMC4284021 or pmid:24786356) and populate baseline field.

issues.issue: SBP change of +1.69 mmHg (f_73f043d9486743) comes from 600 mg supratherapeutic dose at Day 14, not the phase 3 dose (130 mg). The calculator correctly notes this limitation, but the BP harm factor (1.022) may overestimate risk at therapeutic dose. Verified fact f_786c481b4f5067 states "not likely to be associated with any significant change in blood pressure" at 100 mg + atorvastatin.
issues.request: Add a caveat to the calculator input or assumptions that the SBP harm factor is derived from supratherapeutic dose; consider sensitivity analysis with SBP change = 0 for therapeutic dose.

issues.issue: Hypothesis "target_not_causal" against-clause cites REVEAL anacetrapib benefit (9% RRR, HR 0.91) without a fact reference. Should be supported by a verified fact.
issues.request: Add a verified fact for REVEAL anacetrapib outcome (HR 0.91, median 4.1 years) or remove the unsupported claim.

issues.issue: Phase 3 biomarker data exists (HDL-C 129% f_02746d884f6ab5, LDL-C -14% f_342c58c5ac1a94, LDL-C -36% f_fdb5153ab0027b) but calculator uses phase 2 data per protocol. This is correct per instructions, but the large discrepancy between phase 2 LDL-C (-15%) and phase 3 LDL-C (-14% to -36%) should be noted as a caveat.
issues.request: Add a note in calculator assumptions about phase 3 biomarker differences: phase 3 showed LDL-C reduction of -14% (f_342c58c5ac1a94) to -36% (f_fdb5153ab0027b) vs phase 2 -15%, and HDL-C 54-129% vs phase 2 103%.
